# CLOSTRIDIOIDES DIFFICILE INFECTION (CDI)

# Initial CDI diagnosis (all are required)

(1) Unexplained diarrhea (e.g., no laxative or increase in tube feed)

(2) New onset diarrhea (e.g., 3 or more unformed stools in 24 hours)

(3) Laboratory confirmation of CDI

[Click here Information on C. difficile lab testing](orzid2-gmenu-abx-c-difficile-2-step-testing)

The Infectious Disease service is available to discuss CDI testing and results.

# Recurrence

Typically defined as symptomatic, laboratory confirmed CDI within 12 weeks after

a prior episode. Recurrence rates are up to 25%. Recurrence is usually due to

failure of normal colonic flora to re-establish itself, rather than

antimicrobial treatment failure.

# Fulminant CDI

Hypotension, shock, ileus, megacolon: General Surgery consult is essential for

ileus or megacolon.
